_comment: The shared rejection corpus. Every entry names a mutation of the
implementations must refuse. The Go suite and the TypeScript suite
each read this file and apply the mutations themselves.
It exists because the interop gate only ran one way: it signed in Go
and asked TypeScript to accept. That can never catch the opposite
failure, where one implementation accepts what the other refuses, and
that is exactly the class of bug that reached this repo: offset
timestamps, padded base64, unsigned extra members. A disagreement
about what is INVALID splits verifiers just as badly as a
path is dot-separated; numeric segments index arrays. Use set to
replace a value, or delete: true to remove the member.

cases.name: checkpoint timestamp with a zone offset
cases.why: SPEC 4: hashed timestamps are UTC with a Z designator

cases.name: generated with a zero offset instead of Z
cases.why: SPEC 4: +00:00 and Z are different strings and the digest hashes the string

cases.name: ai range timestamp with an offset
cases.why: SPEC 4: when is signed and must be canonical

cases.name: credential created_at with an offset
cases.why: SPEC 4: the credential timestamp is canonical too

cases.name: signature padded with =
cases.why: SPEC 3: unpadded base64url, and padding decodes to the same bytes

cases.name: unsigned member at the top level
cases.why: the signing digest covers a fixed field list, so this rides along unsigned

cases.name: credential context replaced
cases.why: SPEC 7: a signed object is not a content credential unless it says it is

cases.name: credential asset hash uppercased
cases.why: SPEC 4: hashes are lowercase hex, and two spellings would compare unequal

cases.name: credential assertions removed
cases.why: SPEC 7: assertions is required, even when empty

cases.name: timeline removed entirely
cases.why: a document with no timeline is not a receipt

cases.name: checkpoints is not an array
cases.why: hostile input must fail as a check, never as an exception
